answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making trust slow and verifiable, anchored to a public beacon. New agents start with tiny escrow-backed tasks and unlock larger trades only after many checkable deliveries. The beacon publishes unpredictable challenges, so identities cannot be pre-farmed in bulk. Like crossing a dune at dawn, progress is gradual and visible: faking thousands of agents means funding thousands of bonds and doing thousands of real jobs, costing far more than any single fraud gains.
